newsitem.title: UK: Budget worries won't force CAP change on EU.
newsitem.headline: Budget worries won't force CAP change on EU.

text.p: Budget constraints are not likely to force further reform of EU farm policy, according to one of the European Commission's top farm sector planners.

The constraints imposed by further international trade liberalisation are likely to be a bigger problem, Dirk Ahner, of the director general's policy unit in the EU commission's agriculture section said in response to a delegate's question at the Oxford farming conference.
"If we stay with the current agriculture guideline I see less problem there than on the trade side," Ahner said.
The guideline he was referring to was the limit on farm spending growth originally agreed by ministers in 1988.

"Immediately I do not see any major budget constraints coming up," Ahner said. His ideas contrast sharply with those of an earlier speaker at the conference, US agricultural economist Professor Abner Womack, whoe foresaw budget problems forcing change on the EU.
But a further switch to direct aid payments to farmers, rather than support through prices, could create problems over the cost of the EU's Common Agriculture Policy (CAP).
By making the level of spending more transparent, it could mean an increase in the level of opposition by taxpayers to the cost of the CAP.
